audit.why: 48.74% over 2066 games with an EVEN label and Sion holding Levels 2-3 and both item stages is consistent: two tanks who never cleanly solo-kill, with Sion holding the longer arm and Malphite holding Level 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns and no ranges anywhere, and the level-6 spike credits R with 'interrupting a charging Q' while the late-game text tells you never to spend it that way — the page contradicts itself.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is 10/9/8/7/6s. Roar of the Slayer is 12/11/10/9/8s at 800 range. Unstoppable Onslaught is 140/100/60s. Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s at 1000 range. With those numbers the advice resolves: R is worth 130 seconds only on a kill or a carry, never on a charge you can sidestep for free.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into the early text, the spike cards and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Roar of the Slayer is called a 'shield-break missile' in three places — it breaks no shields. What it actually does is reduce Armor, which matters enormously here because Ground Slam's damage is based on Malphite's Armor. The page also never mentions that the missile stops on the first enemy hit, so a minion body-blocks it.
audit.why: Riot text, Roar of the Slayer: 'fires a short range shockwave that damages and slows and reduces the Armor of the first enemy hit. If the shockwave hits a minion or monster, it will be knocked back...'. Ground Slam: 'deals magic damage based on his Armor.'
audit.corrected: His E shreds your armour and therefore your Ground Slam damage, and it dies on the first body it touches — keep a minion in the line.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late breakdown says 'anti-heal stays core' with no reason attached.
audit.why: Here the claim is actually true, and _missing-interactions.json flags it: Glory in Death makes Sion's post-death attacks 'heal him, and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health'. Stating the mechanic makes the item purchase make sense, and it also tells you not to brawl the zombie as a health-stacking tank.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal is justified by Glory in Death, and the zombie's damage scales off your max health — walk away from it rather than fighting it.

edits.before: Two slow tanks, but Sion has the longer arm early — his E is a ranged shield-break missile and a fully-charged Q knockup punishes you if you walk into its line, so at Levels 1-2 you have no answer and just eat poke. Do not contest the wave standing still; you have no trade pattern until W/E. Keep moving sideways so his Q charge never catches you, last-hit at max range, and let Granite Shield refresh between his pokes rather than tanking a full E in the face.
edits.after: Two slow tanks, but Sion has the longer arm — Roar of the Slayer (E) is an 800-range missile that slows and shreds your armour, and a fully-charged Decimating Smash (Q, 10s) knocks you up if you stand in its line. That missile stops on the first thing it hits, so keeping a minion between you costs him the cast outright. Sidestep the charge, last-hit at range, and let Granite Shield refresh instead of tanking pokes.

edits.before: At 4-5 your W armor buff and E shockwave finally let you farm through his poke instead of just absorbing it — sit on the wave, pop W for the splash autos, and your Granite Shield soaks his E. Level 6 is your single edge in this mirror: he is immobile and telegraphs his Q, so R interrupts a charging knockup or flanks him off his zombie reset for a real swing. Bait his E onto the minions, then step up.
edits.after: At 4-5 Thunderclap and Ground Slam finally let you farm through his poke instead of absorbing it. Watch the order though: Roar of the Slayer reduces your armour, and Ground Slam's damage is based on your armour, so if his E lands first yours hits softer. Level 6 is your single edge — he is immobile and telegraphs the charge. Bait the E into a minion, then step up and knock him up.

edits.before: This stays even because neither tank ever cleanly solo-kills the other — you both build armor, both want to start the fight, and his zombie passive lets him keep shoving and deny your CS even after you "win" a trade. The lane is decided by R: yours is a multi-man flank engage, his is a screen-wide knockup, so whoever lands it first in a teamfight wins the exchange. Save R for his carries, not for him, and don't waste it interrupting a Q you can simply walk out of.
edits.after: This stays even because neither tank cleanly solo-kills the other — you both build armour, both want to start the fight, and Glory in Death lets him keep shoving after you "win" a trade. Don't brawl the zombie: its attacks heal him and deal bonus damage based on your maximum health, which is the stat you stack. Walk away and let it expire. Save R for his carries, not for him, and never spend a 130-second ultimate on a Q you can walk out of.

notes: Fabrication removed: Roar of the Slayer was called a 'shield-break missile' in three places. Nothing in Riot's text breaks shields — it reduces Armor, which is the interaction that actually matters, because Ground Slam's damage is based on Malphite's Armor. So Sion's E cuts your damage as well as your durability, and the order of casts decides the trade. Second addition, also absent: the missile stops on the first enemy hit, so a single minion in the line body-blocks it. Third: Glory in Death's attacks heal Sion and deal bonus damage based on the target's maximum health, which both justifies the anti-heal item line the page asserted without reason and tells a health-stacking Malphite to walk away from the zombie rather than brawl it. Flag caution: _missing-interactions.json also claims 'Sion bypasses stacking resistances (Glory in Death (P), Soul Furnace (W))'. The passive's max-health damage is in Riot's text and I used it; the Soul Furnace half appears to come from the max-health-on-kill line rather than any resistance bypass, so I did not assert it. Malphite's own Q/E 'grounding' flags remain unsupported by Riot's descriptions and were not used.
